History and Physical (H&P – Detailed)

Consult Summary:
39-year-old man with sudden onset severe left-sided headache awakening him at 05:30 today; clinical picture most consistent with migraine versus tension-type headache; treated empirically with ibuprofen and lifestyle measures, follow-up arranged in 1 week.

History:
• Presenting complaint: Severe left-sided headache.  
• Onset: Awoke from sleep ≈05:30 today (4–5 h before call).  
• Course: Constant; still present during consult.  
• Character: “Really horrible,” worse than any prior headache; previously experienced milder frontal headaches.  
• Exacerbating/relieving: Initially sore on lying down but then eases somewhat; paracetamol gave no relief.  
• Associated symptoms: Mild photophobia; brief dizziness on rising (resolved).  
• Pertinent negatives: No neck stiffness, no fever, no nausea/vomiting, no focal neurological deficits reported.  
• Triggers/stressors: Significant work stress and late nights ≈2 months.

Past Medical History:
• Generalised anxiety disorder – 2 years, stable.  
• Recurrent mild frontal headaches (historical).

Medications:
• Sertraline – dose/route/frequency not documented.  
• Paracetamol (single dose this morning) – dose/route/frequency not documented.  
Allergies: No known drug allergies.

Social History:
• Lives with partner; owns a cat.  
• Occupation: Not stated; currently under heavy workload.  
• Exercise: Runs ~3×/week.  
• Smoking: Non-smoker.  
• Alcohol/substance use: Not discussed.  
• Sleep: Reduced (late nights).  
• Diet: “OK,” not especially healthy or unhealthy.

Family History:
• Mother with anxiety.  
• No family history of migraine or other significant illness.

Physical Examination:
• Vitals: Not recorded (telephone consult).  
• General/neurological: No examination performed; patient denies red-flag neurological symptoms.

Investigations:
• None performed/ordered at this visit.

Assessment & Plan:

Overall Impression:
Acute unilateral headache most consistent with migraine without aura; tension component possible. Serious secondary causes appear unlikely by history but remain on safety-net list.

DDx Integration:
1. Migraine without aura – unilateral severe pain, photophobia, stress/sleep-deprivation trigger; no focal deficits.  
2. Tension-type headache – ongoing work stress and anxiety, prior frontal “band-like” headaches; less typical due to unilateral location.  
3. Cluster headache – early-morning unilateral pain; lacks autonomic features (low likelihood).

Issue 1 – Acute Headache (probable migraine):
• Assessment: Sudden severe left-sided headache; mild photophobia; no red flags elicited on history.  
• Plan:  
  – Start ibuprofen (high-dose per migraine first-line guidance) – specific dose instructions to be provided in written summary.  
  – May continue paracetamol as needed.  
  – Provide written list of “red-flag” symptoms (e.g., sudden worsening, neurological deficit, vomiting) and advise immediate re-contact or ED if they occur.  
  – Schedule follow-up tele-appointment in 1 week; if no improvement, consider blood tests and/or in-person examination.

Issue 2 – Stress/Anxiety management:
• Assessment: Work-related stress likely contributing to headache frequency/severity.  
• Plan:  
  – Recommend self-certified sick leave up to 1 week to reduce workload.  
  – Provide link for local counselling service (self-referral).  
  – Reinforce ongoing use of sertraline; monitor mental health.

Issue 3 – Lifestyle contributors (sleep, hydration):
• Assessment: Sub-optimal sleep and possible dehydration can precipitate headaches.  
• Plan:  
  – Target ≥7–8 h sleep nightly.  
  – Encourage 1.5–2 L non-caffeinated fluids daily.  
  – Continue regular exercise as tolerated.

General plan items:
• Safety net: Lower threshold to seek care if headache worsens, new symptoms develop, or concerns arise.  
• Documentation: Consultation summary and educational links to be sent to patient portal.

Quality checks:
● Missing expected elements: No vital signs obtained; medication doses/frequencies not documented.  
● Transcript vs DDx conflicts: None significant (DDx supports migraine/tension; aligns with plan).  
● Transcript quality: Clear audio; no noted inaudible sections.
